content.text:
The campaign is finished and submitted. My pick is **index 54** (Bi 0.12, Fe 0.62, V 0.26), which gave the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured: 1.0e-7 A. The best composition in the library is unknown, so this may be well short of the true optimum.

- **Why the Fe-rich side:** the light is 2.06 eV, below BiVO4's band gap of about 2.4 eV. BiVO4 alone should therefore absorb little, so I looked for iron phases that absorb at this energy. XRD on index 54 shows hematite together with BiVO4.
- **Index 55** (Bi 0.28, Fe 0.32, V 0.40) contains BiVO4 by XRD and gave 9e-8 A, slightly below index 54. That gap is small and may be within noise.
- **Index 4** (V-rich, Bi 0.13, Fe 0.28, V 0.59) gave 0 A.
- **Index 113** (Bi-rich) showed different Bi-oxide phases by XRD. I didn't spend a photocurrent measurement on it.

Every sample has peaks that match the tin-oxide substrate; I treated them as background.

**Budget:** all 3 photocurrent measurements are spent, and I used 4 of the 5 XRD scans. With three points I couldn't search the Fe-rich region properly, so an untested composition with more iron could beat index 54.
